learning_outcomes.text: Understand and use the fundamental physical principles of Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Fields and Waves, and Electromagnetism in the analysis and study of concepts and in solving problems associated with higher-level courses.
Identify and evaluate the physical aspects related to Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Fields and Waves, and Electromagnetism present in engineering problems and situations.
Use and relate the different units of measurement for the main physical quantities related to Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Fields and Waves, and Electromagnetism.
Use appropriate measuring instruments to determine the most relevant physical parameters in the fields of Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Fields and Waves, and Electromagnetism.
Acquire experimental skills to verify physical laws and determine physical parameters.
Know how to document a measurement process regarding its foundation, the required instrumentation, and the conditions under which it is valid.
Know how to transmit information, ideas, and conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Second Law of Thermodynamics. Heat engines and motors.
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of two written tests and the completion of laboratory practicals. Laboratory practicals are mandatory and not recoverable. For recovery, a single test covering all course topics (1 to 8 inclusive) will account for 85% of the final grade. The remaining 15% will be the grade obtained in the laboratory practicals.
